This institution assisted the Asantehene and served as an advisory body to the king. The council was made up of [Amanhene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amanhene "Amanhene") or paramount chiefs who were leaders of the various Asante states. The council also included other provincial chiefs. By law the Asantehene never ignored the decisions of the Asanteman council. Doing so could get him de-stooled from the throne.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Empire#cite_note-:concise-104)[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Empire#cite_note-:seth-95)

The Asante Empire was made up of metropolitan and provincial states. The metropolitan states were made up of Asante citizens known as _amanfo_. The provincial states were other kingdoms absorbed into the empire. Every metropolitan Asante state was headed by the _Amanhene_ or paramount chief. Each of these paramount chiefs served as principal rulers of their own states, where they exerted executive, legislative and judicial powers.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Empire#cite_note-:concise-104)

The _Ohene_ is a male representative of his mother's family, where he is chosen from. The _Ohene_ were divisional chiefs under the Amanhene. Their major function was to advise the Amanhene. The divisional chiefs were the highest order in various Asante state divisions. The divisions were made up of various villages put together. Examples of divisional chiefs included Krontihene, Nifahene, Benkumhene, Adontenhene and Kyidomhene.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Empire#cite_note-:concise-104)

Each village in Asante had a chief called Odikro who was the owner of the village. The Odikro was responsible for the maintenance of law and order. He also served as a medium between the people of his jurisdiction, the ancestor and the gods. As the head of the village, the Odikro presided over the village council.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Empire#cite_note-:concise-104)[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Empire#cite_note-:seth-95)

[![Image 24](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/bc/Yaa_Asantewaa_Museum_%284%29.jpg/250px-Yaa_Asantewaa_Museum_%284%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Yaa_Asantewaa_Museum_(4).jpg)

Queen [Yaa Asantewaa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yaa_Asantewaa "Yaa Asantewaa") led her state, [Ejisu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ejisu "Ejisu"), in the [War of the Golden Stool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War_of_the_Golden_Stool "War of the Golden Stool") against the British.

The queen or _Ohenemaa_ was an important figure in Asante political systems. She was the most powerful female in the Empire, because the Ohene represents her or her family and is either her son or her sister's son. She has the power to be King, if she desires but would rather see her son or her maternal nephew(which is also considered her 2nd child in African culture). She had the prerogative of being consulted in the process of installing a chief or the king, as she played a major role in the nomination and selection. She settled disputes involving women and was involved in decision-making alongside the Council of elders and chiefs.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Empire#cite_note-:concise-104) Not only did she participate in the judicial and legislative processes, but also in the making and unmaking of war, and the distribution of land.[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Empire#cite_note-105)

Successful entrepreneurs who accumulated large wealth and men as well as distinguished themselves through heroic deeds were awarded social and political recognition by being called "Abirempon" or "Obirempon" which means big men. By the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries AD, the appellation "Abirempon" had formalized and politicized to embrace those who conducted trade from which the whole state benefited. The state rewarded entrepreneurs who attained such accomplishments with Mena (elephant tail) which was the "heraldic badge"[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Empire#cite_note-FOOTNOTEObeng199623-106)_Obirempon_ s had a fair amount of legislative power in their regions, more than the local nobles of Dahomey but less than the regional governors of the Oyo Empire. In addition to handling the region's administrative and economic matters, the _obirempon_ also acted as the Supreme Judge of their jurisdiction, presiding over court cases.

The Kotoko was a government council in the Asante government. Politically, the kotoko council served as the counterweight to the king's council of elders and basically embodied the aristocratic party in the government. The council formed the Legislature of Asante governmental system.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Empire#cite_note-Edgerton,_Robert_B._1995-1) It was made up of the Asantehene, the Queen mother as well as the state chiefs and their ministers.

The [election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Election "Election") of Kings and the Asantehene (_King of Kings or emperor_ ) himself followed a pattern. The senior female of the kingly lineage nominated the eligible males. This senior female then consulted the elders, male and female, of that line. The final candidate is then selected. That nomination was sent to a council of elders, who represented other lineages in the [town](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Town "Town") or [district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/District "District").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

The Elders then presented the nomination to the assembled people. If the assembled [citizens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citizenship "Citizenship") disapproved of the nominee, the process was restarted.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Empire#cite_note-107) Chosen, the new Kings were enstooled by the Elders, who admonished him with expectations. The chosen Kings swore a solemn oath to the Earth Goddess and to his ancestors to fulfill his duties honorably in which he ["sacrificed"](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sacrifice "Sacrifice") himself and his life for the betterment of the state.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

This elected King enjoyed a [ceremony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ceremony "Ceremony"). He reigned with much power, including the ability to make judgments of life and death on his subjects. However, he did not enjoy [absolute rule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absolute_rule "Absolute rule"). Upon the stool, the King was sacred. He served as the holy intermediary between the people and the ancestors. His powers were theoretically more apparent and hinged on his attention to the advice and decisions of the Council of Elders.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

Kings of the Asante Empire who violated any of the [oaths](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oath_of_office "Oath of office") taken during his or her enstoolment, were destooled by Kingmakers.[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Empire#cite_note-FOOTNOTEObeng199632-108) For instance, if a king punished citizens arbitrarily or was exposed as corrupt, he would be destooled. Destoolment entailed kingmakers removing the sandals of the king and bumping his buttocks on the ground three times. Once destooled from office, his sanctity and thus reverence were lost, as he could not exercise any of the powers he had as king; this includes Chief administrator, Judge, and Military Commander. The now previous king was dispossessed of the Stool, swords and other [regalia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regalia "Regalia") which symbolized his office and authority.

He also lost his position as custodian of the land. However, even if destooled from office, the king remained a member of the royal family from which he was elected.[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Empire#cite_note-FOOTNOTEObeng199632-108) An impeachment occurred during the reign of [Kusi Obodom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kusi_Obodom "Kusi Obodom"), caused by a [failed invasion of Dahomey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Atakpam%C3%A9 "Battle of Atakpamé").[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Empire#cite_note-109)

The _Asantehene_ was assisted by a civil service of men talented in [trade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trade "Trade"), [diplomacy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diplomacy "Diplomacy"), and the [military](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military "Military"), with a head called the _Gyaasehene_. Men from the [Arabian Peninsula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arabian_Peninsula "Arabian Peninsula"), [Sudan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sudan "Sudan"), and [Europe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Europe "Europe") were employed in the Asante empire [civil service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civil_service "Civil service"); all of whom were appointed by the _Asantehene_.[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Empire#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDavidson1991240-110)

[![Image 25](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c6/Brit_Mus_13sept10_brooches_etc_062.jpg/250px-Brit_Mus_13sept10_brooches_etc_062.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Brit_Mus_13sept10_brooches_etc_062.jpg)

Akan drum

The Asante invented the [Fontomfrom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fontomfrom "Fontomfrom"), an Asante [talking drum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talking_drum "Talking drum"), and they also invented the [Akan Drum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akan_Drum "Akan Drum"). They drummed messages to distances of over 300 kilometres (200 mi), as rapidly as a [telegraph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telegraphy "Telegraphy"). [Asante dialect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_dialect "Asante dialect") (Twi) and [Akan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akan_language "Akan language"), the language of the [Asante people](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_people "Asante people") is tonal and more meaning is generated by tone. The drums reproduced these tones, punctuations, and the accents of a phrase so that the cultivated ear heard the entirety of the phrase itself.

The Asante readily heard and understood the phrases produced by these "talking drums". Standard phrases called for meetings of the chiefs or to arms, warned of danger, and broadcast announcements of the death of important figures. Some drums were used for [proverbs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proverb "Proverb") and ceremonial presentations.[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Empire#cite_note-111)

Although pre-literate, the Asante recruited literate individuals into its government to increase the efficiency of the state's diplomacy. Some written records were also kept.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Empire#cite_note-112)[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Empire#cite_note-diplomacy_case_Asante-113) Historian Adjaye, gives estimates based on surviving letters by the Asante that documents from the Asante government "could have exceeded several thousands."[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Empire#cite_note-diplomacy_case_Asante-113) Writing was also used in record keeping during [court proceedings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Court_proceeding "Court proceeding"). Bowdich documented in the early nineteenth century about the "trial of Apea Nyano" on 8 July 1817 where he states that "the [Moorish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moorish "Moorish") secretaries were there to take notes of the transactions of the day." Wilks adds that such transcripts have not survived today.[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Empire#cite_note-114)

Before the 19th century, [couriers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Couriers "Couriers") were trained to memorize the exact contents of the verbal message and by the 19th century, the Asante government relied on writing for diplomacy. In the 1810s, it was common for couriers to be deployed with [despatch boxes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Despatch_box "Despatch box").[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Empire#cite_note-115) For Wilks, evidence exists on the use of mounted couriers during the reign of [Kwaku Dua I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kwaku_Dua_I "Kwaku Dua I") around the Metropolitan districts. He cites a case In 1841 when [Freeman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Birch_Freeman "Thomas Birch Freeman") documented the arrival of a party of messengers sent by the Asantehene to [Kaase](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaase,_Kumasi "Kaase, Kumasi"). The chief of these messengers "rode on a strong Asante pony, with an Arabic or Moorish [saddle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saddle "Saddle") and [bridle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bridle "Bridle")." Wilks argues the tsetse fly nullified the extensive use of horses to speed communications.[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Empire#cite_note-116)

The _Pramakeseso_

or Great Court served as the abode where the Council of Kumasi assembled. Marie-Joseph Bennet documented in the 1870s that "The meeting of the supreme court of justice and legislation takes place every day in the great court of the royal palace called Apramosso (Pramakeseso)." The court measured 30 to 35 meters long by 14 to 15 meters wide.[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Empire#cite_note-Wilks_1989_pp._377%E2%80%938-118)

[Okomfo Anokye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Okomfo_Anokye "Okomfo Anokye") was responsible for creating the **Seventy-Seven Laws of Komfo Anokye** which served as the [codified](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Codification_(law) "Codification (law)") constitution of the Ashanti Empire.[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Empire#cite_note-119)[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Empire#cite_note-120)[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Empire#cite_note-121)

The Asante state, in effect, was a [theocracy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theocracy "Theocracy"). It invokes religious, rather than [secular](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secularity "Secularity")-legal postulates. What the modern state views as [crimes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crime "Crime"), Ashanti view practically as [sins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sin "Sin"). Antisocial acts disrespect the ancestors, and are only secondarily harmful to the [community](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Community "Community"). If the chief or [King](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King "King") fails to punish such acts, he invokes the anger of the ancestors and the gods, and is therefore in danger of [impeachment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Impeachment "Impeachment"). The penalty for some crimes (sins) is death, but this is seldom imposed; a more common penalty is [banishment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exile "Exile") or [imprisonment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Incarceration "Incarceration").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] The King typically exacts or [commutes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commutation_of_sentence "Commutation of sentence") all [capital cases](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capital_punishment "Capital punishment"). These commuted sentences by King and chiefs sometimes occur by [ransom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ransom "Ransom") or [bribe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bribery "Bribery"); they are regulated in such a way that they should not be mistaken for [fines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fine_(penalty) "Fine (penalty)"), but are considered as [revenue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Revenue "Revenue") to the state, which for the most part welcomes [quarrels](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/quarrel "wikt:quarrel") and [litigation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lawsuit "Lawsuit"). [Commutations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commutation_of_sentence "Commutation of sentence") tend to be far more frequent than [executions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capital_punishment "Capital punishment").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

Asante are repulsed by [murder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Murder "Murder"), and [suicide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suicide "Suicide") is considered murder. They decapitate those who commit suicide, the conventional punishment for murder. The suicide thus had contempt for the court, for only the King may kill an Asante.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

In a [murder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Murder "Murder")[trial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trial "Trial"), intent must be established. If the [homicide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homicide "Homicide") is accidental, the murderer pays compensation to the lineage of the deceased. The [insane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insanity "Insanity") cannot be executed because of the absence of responsible intent – except for murder or cursing the King; in the case of cursing the king, drunkenness is a valid defense. [Capital crimes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capital_punishment "Capital punishment") include murder, [incest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Incest "Incest") within the female or male line, and intercourse with a [menstruating](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Menstrual_cycle "Menstrual cycle") woman, [rape](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rape "Rape") of a married woman, and [adultery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adultery "Adultery") with any of the wives of a chief or the King. [Assaults](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assault "Assault") or insults of a chief or the [court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Court "Court") or the King also carried [capital punishment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capital_punishment "Capital punishment").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

Cursing the King, calling down powers to harm the King, is considered an unspeakable act and carries the weight of [death](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Death "Death"). One who invokes another to commit such an act must pay a heavy indemnity. Practitioners of harmful (evil) forms of [sorcery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Witchcraft "Witchcraft") and witchcraft receive death but not by decapitation, for their blood must not be shed. They receive execution by strangling, burning, or drowning.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

Ordinarily, families or lineages settle disputes between individuals. Nevertheless, such disputes can be brought to [trial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trial_(law) "Trial (law)") before a chief by uttering the [taboo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taboo "Taboo") oath of a chief or the King. In the end, the [King's Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Noble_court "Noble court") is the sentencing court, for only the King can order the [death penalty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capital_punishment "Capital punishment"). Before the Council of Elders and the King's Court, the litigants orate comprehensively. Anyone present can cross-examine the defendant or the accuser, and if the proceedings do not lead to a [verdict](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Verdict "Verdict"), a special witness is called to provide additional [testimony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Testimony "Testimony"). If there is only one witness, their sworn oath assures the truth is told. Moreover, that he favours or is hostile to either litigant is unthinkable. Cases with no witness, like sorcery or adultery are settled by ordeals, like drinking [poison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poison "Poison").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

[Ancestor Veneration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Veneration_of_the_dead "Veneration of the dead") establishes the Asante [moral system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morality "Morality"), and it provides the principal foundation for [governmental](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government "Government") sanctions. The link between mother and child centres the entire network, which includes ancestors and fellow men as well. Its [judicial system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judiciary "Judiciary") emphasizes the Asante conception of rectitude and good [behaviour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Behaviour "Behaviour"), which favours harmony among the people. The rules were made by _**Nyame**_ (Supreme [God](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/God "God")) and the ancestors, and one must behave accordingly.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

[![Image 28](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c1/State_Gifts_Presentation_Sword.JPG/250px-State_Gifts_Presentation_Sword.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:State_Gifts_Presentation_Sword.JPG)

Akofena, ceremonial sword used by the Asante

In the metropolitan areas of Asante, several [police forces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_forces "Police forces") were responsible for maintaining law and order. In Kumasi, a uniformed police, who were distinguished by their long hair, maintained order by ensuring no one else entered and left the city without permission from the government.[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Empire#cite_note-122) The _ankobia_ or [special police](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special_police "Special police") were used as the empire's [special forces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special_forces "Special forces") and [bodyguards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bodyguard "Bodyguard") to the Asantehene, as sources of [intelligence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Espionage "Espionage"), and to suppress rebellion.[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Empire#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDavidson1991240-110)

For most of the 19th century and into the 20th century, the Asante [sovereign state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sovereign_state "Sovereign state") remained powerful.[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Empire#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDavidson1991242-123)

[![Image 29](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/83/Lake_Bosumtwi%2C_Ghana.jpg/250px-Lake_Bosumtwi%2C_Ghana.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Lake_Bosumtwi,_Ghana.jpg)

Asante [Mountains](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mountain "Mountain") and [Lake Bosumtwi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Bosumtwi "Lake Bosumtwi"), a natural [lake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake "Lake")

The Asante Empire was one of a series of states along the coast including Dahomey, [Benin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benin "Benin"), and [Oyo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oyo_Empire "Oyo Empire"). The Asante had mountains and large [agricultural](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agriculture "Agriculture") surpluses.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Empire#cite_note-FOOTNOTEObeng199620-3) The southern part of the Asante Empire was covered with moist semi-[deciduous forest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deciduous_forest "Deciduous forest") whilst the [Guinea savanna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guinean_forest-savanna_mosaic "Guinean forest-savanna mosaic") covered the northern part of the state. The Guinea Savanna consists of short deciduous and fire resistant trees. [Riparian forests](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riparian_forest "Riparian forest") also occur along the [Afram River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afram_River "Afram River") and streams of the savanna zone. Soils in Asante were mainly of two types; [forest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forest "Forest") ochrosols in the southern part of Asante whilst the [savanna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Savanna "Savanna") ochrosols were confined to northern part of the empire.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Empire#cite_note-FOOTNOTEObeng199620-3)

The predominant [fauna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fauna "Fauna") or food rich wildlife and animal species encountered in the Asante Empire were the [hen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hen_(bird) "Hen (bird)"), [sheep](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sheep "Sheep"), [goat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goat "Goat"), [duck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duck "Duck"), [turkey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turkey_(bird) "Turkey (bird)"), [rabbit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rabbit "Rabbit"), [guinea fowl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guineafowl "Guineafowl"), [fish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fish "Fish"), and the [porcupine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Porcupine "Porcupine") which became the national emblem of the state, as well as about thirty multipurpose [flora](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flora "Flora") species of trees and [shrubs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shrub "Shrub") and over thirty-five ornamental plants which beautified the environs of Asante. These tree/shrub-crop-animal (hen/fish) components were intensively integrated spatially and/or sequentially on the same land unit of individual Asante houses.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Empire#cite_note-FOOTNOTEObeng199620-3)

The lands within the Asante Kingdom were also rich in river-[gold](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gold "Gold"), [cocoa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cocoa_bean "Cocoa bean") and [kola nuts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kola_nut "Kola nut"), and the Asante were soon trading with the [Portuguese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_Empire "Portuguese Empire") at coastal fort [Sao Jorge da Mina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_Gold_Coast "Portuguese Gold Coast"), later [Elmina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elmina "Elmina"), and with the [Hausa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hausa_people "Hausa people") states.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Empire#cite_note-Britannica-7)

[![Image 30](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/ff/Ashanti_Yam_Ceremony_1817.jpg/250px-Ashanti_Yam_Ceremony_1817.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Ashanti_Yam_Ceremony_1817.jpg)

Asante yam ceremony in the Asante Kingdom, 19th century, by [Thomas E. Bowdich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Edward_Bowdich "Thomas Edward Bowdich").

The Asante prepared the fields by burning before the onset of the rainy season and cultivated with an iron [hoe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hoe_(tool) "Hoe (tool)"). Fields are left fallow for a couple years, usually after two to four years of cultivation. Plants cultivated include [plantains](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plantain_(cooking) "Plantain (cooking)"), [yams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yam_(vegetable) "Yam (vegetable)"), [manioc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cassava "Cassava"), [corn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maize "Maize"), [sweet potatoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sweet_potato "Sweet potato"), [millet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Millet "Millet"), [beans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bean "Bean"), [onions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Onion "Onion"), [peanuts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peanut "Peanut"), [tomatoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tomato "Tomato"), and many [fruits](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fruit "Fruit"). Manioc and corn are New World transplants introduced during the [Atlantic European trade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlantic_slave_trade "Atlantic slave trade"). Many of these [vegetable](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vegetable "Vegetable") crops could be harvested twice a year and the [cassava](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cassava "Cassava") (manioc), after a two-year growth, provides a starchy root.

The Asante transformed [palm wine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palm_wine "Palm wine"), maize and millet into [beer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beer "Beer"), a favourite drink; and made use of the oil from palm for many culinary and domestic uses.[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Empire#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDavidson1991240-110)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Empire#cite_note-Collins_and_Burns-10)

Infrastructure throughout the empire included a network of well-kept [roads](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Road "Road") from the Asante mainland to the [Niger river](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Niger_River "Niger River") and other trade cities.[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Empire#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDavidson1991240-110)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Empire#cite_note-Collins_and_Burns-10) Stationed at various points of Asante roads were the _Nkwansrafo_ or road wardens who served as the highway police; checking the movement of traders and strangers on all roads. They were also responsible for scouting and were charged with the collection of [tolls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toll_road "Toll road") from traders.[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Empire#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWilks198948%E2%80%9355-124)

In the early 19th century larger rivers were either forded in the dry season or crossed by canoe or line-and-raft ferries. Smaller rivers were either waded, or were bridged by a tree trunk: in both cases a rope [handrail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Handrail "Handrail") was usually stretched across the river to assist the traveller. In response to the delivery of a carriage by [Thomas Freeman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Birch_Freeman "Thomas Birch Freeman") in 1841, the Asante Empire began to build [bridges](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bridges "Bridges") across water bodies for transport that year.[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Empire#cite_note-Wilks_1989_38-125) Asantehene [Kwaku Dua](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kwaku_Dua_I "Kwaku Dua I") ordered proper bridges to be built across streams in the metropolitan area of Kumase. Thomas Freeman described the construction as:

> ...some stout, forked sticks or posts are driven in the centre of the stream at convenient distances, across which are placed some strong beams, fastened to the posts with withes, from the numerous climbing plants on every hand. On these bearers are placed long stout poles which are covered with earth from fourth to six inches thick; and this completes the bridge.

—Freeman.[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Empire#cite_note-Wilks_1989_38-125)

English visitors to Kumasi in the 19th century, noted the division of the capital into 77 wards with 27 main streets; one of which was 100 yards wide. Many houses especially those near the king's palace were two story buildings embodied with indoor [plumbing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plumbing "Plumbing") in the form of toilets that were flushed with gallons of boiling water.[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Empire#cite_note-126) Bowdich revealed in his 1817 account that all streets of Kumasi [were named](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Street_name "Street name").[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Empire#cite_note-127)[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Empire#cite_note-128)

The population history of the Asante Kingdom was one of slow centralization. In the early 19th century the Asantehene used the annual tribute to set up a permanent standing army armed with [rifles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rifle "Rifle"), which allowed much closer control of the Asante kingdom. The Asante kingdom was one of the most centralised states in sub-Saharan Africa. Osei Tutu and his successors oversaw a policy of political and cultural unification and the union had reached its full extent by 1750. It remained an alliance of several large city-states which acknowledged the sovereignty of the ruler of Kumasi and the Asante kingdom, known as the Asantehene. The Asante kingdom had a dense population of approximately 3 million people, allowing the creation of substantial [urban centres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urban_centre "Urban centre") across an area of over 250,000 square kilometers.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Empire#cite_note-FOOTNOTEObeng199620-3)

[![Image 31](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/67/Ashanteewarcaptain.jpg/250px-Ashanteewarcaptain.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Ashanteewarcaptain.jpg)

Asante Military [Field Marshal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Field_marshal "Field marshal"), c.1819, by [Thomas E. Bowdich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Edward_Bowdich "Thomas Edward Bowdich")

The Asante armies served the empire well, supporting its long period of expansion and subsequent resistance to European colonization. 

Armament was primarily with firearms, but some historians hold that indigenous organization and leadership probably played a more crucial role in Asante successes.[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Empire#cite_note-Vandervort-129) These are, perhaps, more significant when considering that the Asante had numerous troops from conquered or incorporated peoples, and faced a number of revolts and rebellions from these peoples over its long history. The political genius of the symbolic "golden stool" and the fusing effect of a national army however, provided the unity needed to keep the empire viable. Total potential strength was some 80,000 to 200,000, making the Asante army bigger than the well known Zulu, and comparable to possibly Africa's largest – the legions of Ethiopia.[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Empire#cite_note-Vandervort-129) The Asante army was described as a fiercely organized one whose king could "bring 200,000 men into the field and whose warriors were evidently not cowed by [Snider rifles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snider%E2%80%93Enfield "Snider–Enfield") and 7-pounder guns"[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Empire#cite_note-130)

While actual forces deployed in the field were less than _potential_ strength, tens of thousands of soldiers were usually available to serve the needs of the empire. Mobilization depended on small cadres of regulars, who guided and directed levees and contingents called up from provincial governors.

[![Image 32](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/78/Adoo_Quamina%2C_1820_by_William_Hutton.jpg/250px-Adoo_Quamina%2C_1820_by_William_Hutton.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Adoo_Quamina,_1820_by_William_Hutton.jpg)

An Asante captain depicted in an 1820 [aquatint](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aquatint "Aquatint") by [William Hutton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Hutton_(colonial_administrator) "William Hutton (colonial administrator)")

Organization was structured around an advance guard, main body, rear guard and two right and left wing flanking elements. This provided flexibility in the forest country the Asante armies typically operated in. Horses were known to survive in Kumasi but because they could not survive in the tsetse fly-infested forest zone in the south, there was no cavalry. Asante high-ranking officers rode horses with the hauteur of European officers but they did not ride to battle.[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Empire#cite_note-131) The approach to the battlefield was typically via converging columns, and tactics included ambushes and extensive maneuvers on the wings. Unique among African armies, the Asante deployed medical units to support their fighters. This force was to expand the empire substantially and continually for over a century, and defeated the British in several encounters.[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Empire#cite_note-Vandervort-129)

Brass barrel blunderbuss were produced in some states in the Gold Coast including the Asante Empire around the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries. Various accounts indicate that Asante blacksmiths were not only able to repair firearms, but that barrels, locks and stocks were on occasion remade.[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Empire#cite_note-RA_Kea1971-132)

## Culture and society

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Asante_Empire&action=edit&section=51 "Edit section: Culture and society")]

[![Image 33](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2f/The_National_Archives_UK_-_CO_1069-31-28.jpg/250px-The_National_Archives_UK_-_CO_1069-31-28.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:The_National_Archives_UK_-_CO_1069-31-28.jpg)

Ashanti architecture (exterior house) Coomassie (Kumasi).c.1873

Standing among families was largely political. The royal family typically topped the hierarchy, followed by the families of the [chiefs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tribal_chiefs "Tribal chiefs") of territorial divisions. In each [chiefdom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chiefdom "Chiefdom"), a particular female line provides the chief. A committee of several men eligible for the post elects the chief. The typical Asante family was [extended](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extended_family "Extended family") and [matrilineal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matrilineal "Matrilineal").[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Empire#cite_note-133) A mother's brother was the legal guardian of her children. The father on the other hand had fewer legal responsibilities for his children with the exception of ensuring their well-being. Women also had the right to initiate [divorce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Divorce "Divorce") whiles the husband had some legal rights over his wife such as the right to cut off her nose for adultery.[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Empire#cite_note-134)

Prominent people wore silk. The ordinary Asante wore cotton whiles slaves dressed in black cloth. Garments signalled the rank of the wearer in society and its colour expressed different meanings. White was worn by ordinary people after winning a court case. Dark colours were worn for funerals or mourning.[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Empire#cite_note-Edgerton_page_41-42-135) Laws existed to restrict certain Kente designs to the nobility. Some cotton or silk patterns on the Kente were designed solely for the king and could only be worn with his permission.[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Empire#cite_note-Edgerton_page_41-42-135)

### Education and children

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Asante_Empire&action=edit&section=54 "Edit section: Education and children")]

[![Image 34](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/90/Aquasi_Boachi_and_Quamin_Poko_by_JL_Cornet.jpg/250px-Aquasi_Boachi_and_Quamin_Poko_by_JL_Cornet.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Aquasi_Boachi_and_Quamin_Poko_by_JL_Cornet.jpg)

Princes [Kwasi Boakye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kwasi_Boakye "Kwasi Boakye") and Kwame Poku, c.1840.

Education in the Asante Kingdom was conducted by Asante and imported scholars and Asante people would often attend schools in Europe for their [higher education](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Higher_education "Higher education").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

Tolerant parents are typical among the Asante. Childhood is considered a happy time and children cannot be responsible for their actions. The child is not responsible for their actions until after [puberty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puberty "Puberty"). A child is harmless and there is no worry for the control of their [soul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soul_(spirit) "Soul (spirit)"), the original purpose of all [funeral rites](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Funeral "Funeral"), so the ritual funerals typically given to the deceased Asante are not as lavish for the children.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

The Asante adored twins when they were born within the [royal family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_family "Royal family") because they were seen as a sign of impending fortune. Ordinarily, boy twins joined the army and twin girls potential wives of the King. If the twins are a boy and girl, no particular career awaits them. Women who bear [triplets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multiple_birth "Multiple birth") are greatly honored because three is regarded as a lucky number. Special [rituals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ritual "Ritual") ensue for the third, sixth, and ninth child. The fifth child (unlucky five) can expect misfortune. Families with many children are well respected and barren women scoffed at.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

The Asante used [Adinkra symbols](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adinkra_symbols "Adinkra symbols") in their daily society. The symbols were used as a form of decoration, logos, arts, sculpture and pottery.

### Menstruation and impurity

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Asante_Empire&action=edit&section=56 "Edit section: Menstruation and impurity")]

[![Image 35](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/97/The_National_Archives_UK_-_CO_1069-34-31-2-001.jpg/330px-The_National_Archives_UK_-_CO_1069-34-31-2-001.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:The_National_Archives_UK_-_CO_1069-34-31-2-001.jpg)

An Asante fetish temple in the village of Jufu by the 19th century[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Empire#cite_note-:Pruss_Trad-101)

The Asante held [puberty rites](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puberty_rite "Puberty rite") only for females. Fathers instruct their sons without public observance. The privacy of boys was respected in the Asante kingdom. As [menstruation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Menstruation "Menstruation") approaches, a girl goes to her mother's house. When the girl's menstruation is disclosed, the mother announces the good news in the village beating an iron hoe with a stone. Old women come out and sing _Bara_ (menstrual) songs.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

Menstruating women suffered numerous restrictions. The Asante viewed them as ritually unclean. They did not cook for men, nor did they eat any food cooked for a man. If a menstruating woman entered the ancestral stool (shrine) house, she was arrested, and the punishment could result in death. If this punishment is not exacted, the Asante believe, the ghost of the [ancestors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ancestor "Ancestor") would strangle the [chief](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tribal_chief "Tribal chief"). Menstruating women lived in special houses during their periods as they were forbidden to cross the threshold of men's houses. They swore no [oaths](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oath "Oath") and no oaths were sworn for or against them. They did not participate in any of the [ceremonial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ceremony "Ceremony") observances and did not visit any [sacred](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sacred "Sacred") places.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

### Healthcare and death

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Asante_Empire&action=edit&section=57 "Edit section: Healthcare and death")]

[![Image 36](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/df/Ashanti_soulwasher_by_Claire_H.jpg/250px-Ashanti_soulwasher_by_Claire_H.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Ashanti_soulwasher_by_Claire_H.jpg)

Asante soulwasher

Sickness and death were major events in the [kingdom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monarchy "Monarchy"). The ordinary [herbalist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herbalist "Herbalist") divined the [supernatural](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supernatural "Supernatural") cause of the illness and treated it with [herbal medicines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herbal_medicine "Herbal medicine").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

[![Image 37](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/66/Bonnat_AschantiPriester.jpg/250px-Bonnat_AschantiPriester.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Bonnat_AschantiPriester.jpg)

 A [priest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Priest "Priest") (okomfo) performing an [Akan religious](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akan_religion "Akan religion") ceremony, c.1873, by [Jules Gros](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jules_Gros_(journalist) "Jules Gros (journalist)")

People loathed being alone for long without someone available to perform this rite before the sick collapsed. The family dressed the deceased in their best clothes, and adorned them with packets of gold dust (money for the after-life), ornaments, and food for the journey "up the hill". The body was normally buried within 24 hours. Until that time the funeral party engage in dancing, drumming, shooting of guns, all accompanied by the wailing of relatives. This was done because the Asante typically believed that death was not something to be sad about, but rather a part of life. As the Asante believed in an after-life, families felt they would be reunited with their ancestors upon death. Funeral rites for the death of a king involved the whole kingdom and were a much more elaborate affair.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

The greatest and most frequent [ceremonies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ceremony "Ceremony") of the Asante recalled the spirits of departed rulers with an offering of food and drink, asking their favour for the common good, called the _[Adae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adae\_Festival "Adae Festival")_. The day before the _Adae_, [Akan drums](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akan_Drum "Akan Drum") broadcast the approaching ceremonies. The stool treasurer gathers sheep and liquor that will be offered. The chief priest officiates the _Adae_ in the stool house where the ancestors came. The [priest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Priest "Priest") offers each food and a beverage. The public ceremony occurs outdoors, where all the people joined the dancing. Minstrels chant ritual phrases; the talking drums extol the chief and the ancestors in traditional phrases. The _Odwera_, the other large ceremony, occurs in September and typically lasted for a week or two. It is a time of cleansing of sin from society the defilement, and for the purification of [shrines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shrine "Shrine") of ancestors and the gods. After the [sacrifice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sacrifice "Sacrifice") and feast of a black [hen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hen_(bird) "Hen (bird)")—of which both the living and the dead share—a new year begins in which all are clean, strong, and healthy.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

Slavery was practiced in the Asante Empire, with slaves typically taken as captives from enemies in warfare. The Asante Empire was the largest slaveowning and slave trading state in the territory of today's Ghana during the [Atlantic slave trade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlantic_slave_trade "Atlantic slave trade").[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Empire#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPerbi200423-136) The welfare of their slaves varied from being able to acquire wealth and intermarry with the master's family to being [sacrificed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_sacrifice "Human sacrifice") in funeral ceremonies. The Asante believed that slaves would follow their masters into the afterlife. Slaves could sometimes own other slaves, and could also request a new master if the slave believed he or she was being severely mistreated.[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Empire#cite_note-137)[[138]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Empire#cite_note-138)

The modern-day Asante claim that slaves were seldom abused,[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Empire#cite_note-139) and that a person who abused a slave was held in high contempt by [society](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Society "Society"). They defend the "humanity" of Asante slavery by noting that those slaves were allowed to marry.[[140]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Empire#cite_note-History_of_the_Ashanti_Empire-140) If a master found a female slave desirable, he might marry her. He preferred such an arrangement to that of a free woman in a conventional marriage, because marriage to an enslaved woman allowed the children to inherit some of the father's [property](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Property "Property") and status.[[141]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Empire#cite_note-141)

This favoured arrangement occurred primarily because of what some men considered their conflict with the [matrilineal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matrilineality "Matrilineality") system. Under this kinship system, children were considered born into the mother's clan and took their status from her family.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] Generally her eldest brother served as mentor to her children, particularly for the boys. She was protected by her family.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] Some Asante men felt more comfortable taking a slave girl or pawn wife in marriage, as she would have no _[abusua](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abusua "Abusua")_ (older male grandfather, father, uncle or brother) to intercede on her behalf when the couple argued. With an enslaved wife, the master and husband had total control of their children, as she had no kin in the community.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

During the reign of Asantehene Osei Kwame Panyin (1777–1803), the sale of Asante citizens into slavery was banned. Wilks argues that the economy of Asante "was not one based upon slave-raiding for export purposes". He cites Asantehene Osei Bonsu's speech to Dupuis in 1820;

> I cannot make war to catch slaves in the bush, like a thief. My ancestors never did so. But if I fight a king and kill him when he is insolent, then
> 
> 
> certainly I must have his gold, and his slaves, and the people are mine too. Do not White kings act like this?
> 
> 
> — Osei Bonsu

He also references Brodie Cruickshank, who wrote in 1853 that "The Ashantee wars are never undertaken expressly to supply this demand." Wilks writes that slaves were more important to the Asante economy in the form of domestic labor in the agricultural and industrial sector than for export in the Atlantic slave trade. Some historians such as Reid and Dalrymple-Smith have commented that the Asante economy did not depend on the Atlantic slave trade. Stilwell states that the Asante rulers traded in slaves but "also sought other economic options."

When the Kingdom of Asante was conquered by the British in 1896, the British assured the chiefs that they would be allowed to keep their slaves; Asante became a colony in 1901 and in 1902 it was made illegal to "compel or attempt the compel the services" or another person, but slavery was not explicitly abolished due to British fear that an abolition would cause "internal disorganization"; chattel slavery was formally banned in 1908, but the British authorities did not enforce the law until the 1920s.[[142]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Empire#cite_note-142)

[![Image 38](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/35/M%C3%A1scara_de_oro_-_tesoro_del_rey_Kofi_Kolkalli.jpg/250px-M%C3%A1scara_de_oro_-_tesoro_del_rey_Kofi_Kolkalli.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:M%C3%A1scara_de_oro_-_tesoro_del_rey_Kofi_Kolkalli.jpg)

Golden mask property of [Asantehene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asantehene "Asantehene"), [Kofi Karikari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kofi_Karikari "Kofi Karikari")

Asante Empire's involvement in gold, cloth and slave trades brought in abundant wealth and fostered rich artistic traditions.[[143]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Empire#cite_note-143) During colonization, the British took many artifacts. In February 2024, some of these, on display in a U.S. museum, were returned to Ghana. The repatriation has been termed "the return of our souls" and activists hope that eventually all of the artifacts will be returned.[[144]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Empire#cite_note-144)

[![Image 39](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3a/Ashant_architecture.jpg/250px-Ashant_architecture.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Ashant_architecture.jpg)

Picture of Asante architecture drawn by [Thomas Edward Bowdich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Edward_Bowdich "Thomas Edward Bowdich"), with [Adinkra symbols](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adinkra_symbols "Adinkra symbols") on the walls.

[![Image 40](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/fa/Kumasi.png/250px-Kumasi.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Kumasi.png)

Palace of King Kwaku Dua of Kumasi, [Kumasi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kumasi "Kumasi"), 1887.

The Asante traditional buildings are the only remnants of Asante architecture. Construction and design consisted of a timber framework filled up with clay and [thatched](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thatching "Thatching") with sheaves of leaves. The surviving designated sites are [shrines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shrine "Shrine"), but there have been many other buildings in the past with the same architectural style.[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Empire#cite_note-145) These buildings served as [palaces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palace "Palace") and [shrines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shrine "Shrine") as well as houses for the affluent.[[146]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Empire#cite_note-146) The Asante Empire also built [mausoleums](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mausoleums "Mausoleums") which housed the tombs of several Asante leaders. Generally, houses whether designed for human habitation or for the [deities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deity "Deity"), consisted of four separate rectangular single-room buildings set around an open [courtyard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Courtyard "Courtyard"); the inner corners of adjacent buildings were linked by means of splayed screen walls, whose sides and angles could be adapted to allow for any inaccuracy in the initial layout. Typically, three of the buildings were completely open to the courtyard, while the fourth was partially enclosed, either by the door and windows, or by open-work screens flanking an opening.[[147]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Empire#cite_note-147)

The Asante Empire has been depicted in a number of different works of [nonfiction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Creative_nonfiction "Creative nonfiction"), detailing the structure of the empire

### Literature and theatre

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Asante_Empire&action=edit&section=63 "Edit section: Literature and theatre")]

*   The novel [The Two Hearts of Kwasi Boachi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Two_Hearts_of_Kwasi_Boachi "The Two Hearts of Kwasi Boachi") (1997)[[148]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Empire#cite_note-148) is based on the memoirs of [Kwasi Boachi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kwasi_Boachi "Kwasi Boachi"), the son of the Asantehene [Kwaku Dua I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kwaku_Dua_I "Kwaku Dua I"), from when he and his cousin Kwame Poku were sent to [the Netherlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom_of_the_Netherlands "United Kingdom of the Netherlands") in 1837 to receive a European education.
*   It was later adapted into an opera in 2007 by the author [Arthur Japin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Japin "Arthur Japin") and composer [Jonathan Dove](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jonathan_Dove "Jonathan Dove")[[149]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Empire#cite_note-149)
*   The 2006 novel [Copper Sun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copper_Sun "Copper Sun")'s protagonist Amari comes from the Asante Empire.

*   The singer [Ashanti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashanti_(singer) "Ashanti (singer)") was named after the alternative name 'Ashanti empire'. This is because women had power and influence there, and her mother wanted her to follow that model.[[150]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Empire#cite_note-150)

*   The Asante Empire is referenced in the _[Static Shock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Static\_Shock "Static Shock")_ episodes "Static in Africa" and "Out of Africa", where [Static](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Static_(DC_Comics) "Static (DC Comics)") and his family visit Ghana.

The Asante Empire has been depicted in some historical [war strategy video games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strategy_video_game "Strategy video game"), along with being characters in video games with origins from the area.

*   In the [grand strategy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_strategy_wargame "Grand strategy wargame") video games _[Europa Universalis IV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Europa\_Universalis\_IV "Europa Universalis IV")_ (2013) and _[Victoria 3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victoria\_3 "Victoria 3")_ (2022), both developed by [Paradox Interactive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paradox_Interactive "Paradox Interactive"), the Ashanti Empire appears as one of many historical nations that players can play as or interact with.
*   In _[Crusader Kings III](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crusader\_Kings\_III "Crusader Kings III")_, the Ashanti Empire is one of the many nations that players can play or interact as.
*   In _[Assassin's Creed IV: Black Flag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assassin's\_Creed\_IV:\_Black\_Flag "Assassin's Creed IV: Black Flag")_, two characters, Kumi Berko, a pirate playable in the multiplayer mode under the pseudonym "The Mercenary", and Antó, a Master Assassin of the West Indies Brotherhood, were both born in the Ashanti Empire.
*   The Ashanti Empire appears as a playable minor civilization in _[Age of Empires III](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Age\_of\_Empires\_III "Age of Empires III")_.

[[](https://www.instagram.com/thandiiiii) thandiiiii 71.9K To be anti-African spirituality is to be anti-Black. That’s it. You can’t make final claims on things you don’t know. So many people on the continent and in the Diaspora think their ancestral practices are demonic. And even a lot of people say they know it’s demonic from family experiences — but maybe YOUR grandmother was a witch, practicing witchcraft. But what I can guarantee is if you had ancestors who were Elegbe, Iyalorisa, Babalorisa, Awos, Bokors, Akomfo, etc. they were NOT doing evil work. Majority of traditional African practices are HEALING practices. Sure, like in any religion, there are some bad people who don’t use the traditions correctly, but they are an unaccepted minority. Is evil witchcraft real? Yes. And it does exist in Africa and the Diaspora, but traditional spiritual systems like Ifa and Orisa are not that. It’s something totally different. In fact, we protect ourselves and others against it. The historical FACT is that the demonization of ATRs is a direct result of colonization, slavery, and white supremacy. Does that mean you’re anti-Black if you practice an Abrahamic religion? not in my personal opinion. But on the other side of the coin, if you are so hung up on ATRs being evil because that’s what your church told you, or better yet films from your childhood told you, you got bigger problems to tackle. It’s 2025, we really have to stop believing scary stories about people’s real lives. In Ifa and Orisa, we don’t judge other people’s beliefs, so it’s just so weird when my fellow Black / African people judge something that is literally healing and positive. Especially those of you whose Lord & Savior literally told you, “Do not judge, or you too will be judged” — forreal, WWJD? # Spiritual Leader Helped Form The Ashanti Tribe
[[](https://www.instagram.com/thandiiiii) thandiiiii 71.9K To be anti-African spirituality is to be anti-Black. That’s it. You can’t make final claims on things you don’t know. So many people on the continent and in the Diaspora think their ancestral practices are demonic. And even a lot of people say they know it’s demonic from family experiences — but maybe YOUR grandmother was a witch, practicing witchcraft. But what I can guarantee is if you had ancestors who were Elegbe, Iyalorisa, Babalorisa, Awos, Bokors, Akomfo, etc. they were NOT doing evil work. Majority of traditional African practices are HEALING practices. Sure, like in any religion, there are some bad people who don’t use the traditions correctly, but they are an unaccepted minority. Is evil witchcraft real? Yes. And it does exist in Africa and the Diaspora, but traditional spiritual systems like Ifa and Orisa are not that. It’s something totally different. In fact, we protect ourselves and others against it. The historical FACT is that the demonization of ATRs is a direct result of colonization, slavery, and white supremacy. Does that mean you’re anti-Black if you practice an Abrahamic religion? not in my personal opinion. But on the other side of the coin, if you are so hung up on ATRs being evil because that’s what your church told you, or better yet films from your childhood told you, you got bigger problems to tackle. It’s 2025, we really have to stop believing scary stories about people’s real lives. In Ifa and Orisa, we don’t judge other people’s beliefs, so it’s just so weird when my fellow Black / African people judge something that is literally healing and positive. Especially those of you whose Lord & Savior literally told you, “Do not judge, or you too will be judged” — forreal, WWJD? Calm down & just vibe twin 😎](https://www.instagram.com/reel/DI6UI_KgW-C/?utm_source=popular_topic_grid)

The **Asante Empire** (Asante Twi: _**Asanteman**_), also known as the **Ashanti Empire**, was an Akan state that lasted from 1701 to 1902, in what is now modern-day Ghana.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Empire#cite_note-Britannica-7) It expanded from the Ashanti Region to include most of Ghana and also parts of Ivory Coast and Togo.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Empire#cite_note-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Empire#cite_note-9) Due to the empire's military prowess, wealth, architecture, sophisticated hierarchy, trade networks and culture, the Asante Empire has been extensively studied and has more historic records written by European, primarily British, authors than any other indigenous culture of sub-Saharan Africa.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Empire#cite_note-Collins_and_Burns-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Empire#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMcCaskie20032-11)

Starting in the late 17th century, the Asante king Osei Tutu (c.1695– 1717) and his adviser Okomfo Anokye established the Asante Kingdom, with the Golden Stool of Asante as a sole unifying symbol.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Empire#cite_note-Britannica-7)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Empire#cite_note-12) Osei Tutu oversaw a massive Asante territorial expansion, building up the army by introducing new organisation and turning a disciplined royal and paramilitary army into an effective fighting machine. In 1701, the Asante army conquered Denkyira, giving the Asante access to the Gulf of Guinea and the Atlantic Ocean coastal trade with Europeans, notably the Dutch.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Empire#cite_note-Collins_and_Burns-10) The economy of the Asante Empire was mainly based on the trade of gold and agricultural exports[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Empire#cite_note-Green,_Toby-13) as well as slave trading, craft work and trade with markets further north.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Empire#cite_note-arhin_trade-6)

The Asante Empire fought several wars with neighboring kingdoms and lesser organized groups such as the Fante. The Asante held their own against the British in the first two of the five Anglo-Ashanti Wars, killing British army general Sir Charles MacCarthy and keeping his skull as a gold-rimmed drinking cup in 1824. British forces later burnt and sacked the Asante capital of Kumasi, however, and following the final Asante defeat at the fifth Anglo-Ashanti War, the Asante empire became part of the Gold Coast colony on 1 January 1902. Today, the Asante Kingdom survives as a constitutionally protected, sub-national traditional state[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Empire#cite_note-Roeder-14) in union with the Republic of Ghana. The current king of the Asante kingdom is Otumfuo Osei Tutu II. The Asante kingdom is the home to Lake Bosumtwi, Ghana's only natural lake. The state's current economic revenue is derived mainly from trading in gold bars, cocoa, kola nuts and agriculture.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Empire#cite_note-Collins_and_Burns-10)

### Meaning of the name _Asante_
[edit]
Kente cloth, the traditional garment worn by Asante royalty, has been widely adopted throughout the Asante kingdom.
The name _Asante_ means "because of war". The word derives from the Twi words _ɔsa_ meaning "war" and _nti_ meaning "because of". This name comes from the Asante's origin as a kingdom created to fight the Denkyira kingdom.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Empire#cite_note-15)
The variant name "Ashanti" comes from British reports transcribing "Asante" as the British heard it pronounced, _as-hanti_. The hyphenation was subsequently dropped and the name _Ashanti_ remained, with various spellings including _Ashantee_ common into the early 20th century.

### Amansie and the Five cradles of Akan civilization
[edit]
Akan traditions preserve several types of historical narratives known as _adomankomasem_ (creation stories), _atetesem_ (migration traditions), and _abakomsem_ (histories of political authority).[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Empire#cite_note-FOOTNOTEParker2026228%E2%80%93229-16) In Asante traditions, **Amansie** is remembered as the early homeland of the Akan people and means the "Origin of the Nations" or the "Settlement of the Aborigines." The region was associated with the ancestors of the Aduana and Oyoko clans, who are said to have first settled at Asumennya–Santemanso. One tradition recounts how a golden chain descended from the sky carrying a stool and a herald woman, Ankyewea Nyame, the ancestor of the Oyoko lineage, who settled at Asantemanso where other people later emerged from the earth and joined her community.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Empire#cite_note-FOOTNOTEParker2026228%E2%80%93229-16) From Amansie, a large portion of the Akan population later migrated to Adanse, where permanent settlements were established and the transition from mobile communities to organized political societies began.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Empire#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPrempeh202294%E2%80%9395-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Empire#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPrempeh202294-18) Early Akan political organization developed around communities known as _aman_ (states), which were independent political communities governed by ruling lineages.

### Amansie and the Five cradles of Akan civilization
Authority within the communities was symbolized by the _akonnwa_ (stools), which represented the legitimacy of a chief's right to rule.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Empire#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWilks199391%E2%80%9392-19) The earliest Akan states in the region between the Pra and Ofin rivers were Adansemanso, Abuakwa Atwumamanso, Asenmanso, Abankeseso, and Asantemanso, collectively known as the _Akanman Nnum Piesie_ ("Five First-Born Akan States").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Empire#cite_note-FOOTNOTEParker2026230-20)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Empire#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWilks199391%E2%80%9392-19)
